content.content: 1 # Full spec (verbatim from the user) — supervisor — 2026-11-02 2 3 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. Project's own tests must pass at the end. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 28 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 29 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. 30 - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. 31 - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 32 33 Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 34 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 35 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 36 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 37 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 38 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 39 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 40 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 41 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 42 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 43 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. 44 - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. 45 46 Page 47 - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. 48 - The page loads the script with a `

2	
3	Files: `public/index.html` (served at `GET /`), `public/app.js` (served at `GET /app.js`).
4	
5	## Element ids (all fetched once at startup via document.getElementById)
6	| id | tag / type | notes |
7	|----|-----------|-------|
8	| booking-form | form[novalidate] | listener: `submit` |
9	| room | select[name=room] | starts empty; filled with `<option>` per room |
10	| title | input[type=text][name=title] | emptied on 201 |
11	| date | input[type=date][name=date] | |
12	| start | input[type=time][name=start] | |
13	| end | input[type=time][name=end] | |
14	| book | button[type=submit] `Book` | `disabled` toggled |
15	| filter-date | input[type=date] (label `Show date`) | listener: `change` only |
16	| show-all | button[type=button] `Show all` | listener: `click` |
17	| booking-list | ul | `replaceChildren` on list success |
18	| error | p[role=alert], empty | written via `textContent` |
19	
20	## Browser APIs app.js touches (and nothing else; no other globals)
21	- Globals: `fetch`, `document` only. Classic script wrapped in an IIFE; runs at once.
22	- `document.getElementById(id)`, `document.createElement('option' | 'li' | 'button')`.
23	- `fetch(url, options)` always called with an options object:
24	  - GET: `{ method: 'GET' }`
25	  - POST: `{ method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: <JSON string> }`
26	    body key order: room, title, date, start, end (raw values).
27	  - DELETE: `{ method: 'DELETE' }`
28	- Response: reads `status`; calls `json()` (awaited, may reject) unless status is 204.
29	- Element members used:
30	  - setters: `value` (option, title, filter-date), `textContent` (option, button, #error), `type` (='button' on Cancel), `disabled`
31	  - getters: `value` (room, title, date, start, end, filter-date), `disabled` (book, Cancel button)
32	  - methods: `append(...nodesOrStrings)` (li: `append(text, button)` or `append('No bookings.')`), `replaceChildren(...nodes)` (#room on rooms success, #booking-list on list success), `addEventListener(type, fn)`
33	- Events: `event.preventDefault()` on submit (first statement). Click handlers ignore the event.
34	- Listeners registered: form `submit`, #filter-date `change`, #show-all `click`, each Cancel button `click`.
35	
36	## Startup order
37	`fetch('/api/rooms')` then `fetch('/api/bookings[?date=v]')`, both synchronously during script run (2 calls before any await resolves).
38	
39	## Fake-DOM tips for testing
40	- A fake `textContent` setter should replace children; `append` of a string = text node.
41	- Async: each outcome needs ~2 microtask hops (fetch, json); `await new Promise(r => setImmediate(r))` is enough.
42	- A click on a disabled Cancel button (or submit while Book disabled) sends nothing.
43	- 200 GET with a body lacking an array `rooms` / `bookings` (or non-object bookings) → `#error` = `Request failed.`, list/select untouched (see decisions.md).

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

content.text:
Both files pass. I checked them against every line of the Page section, the reply shapes in the API section, and your hard constraints. I found no spec violations.

**Checks run**
- A search of `/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/public` found none of the forbidden items: `innerHTML`, `createTextNode`, `querySelector`, `setAttribute`, `classList`, `console`, `setTimeout`, `.ok`, `.text()`, `http(s)://`, `import`/`export`, `window`, or `on…=` attributes.
- `node --check` on `app.js` succeeds.

**`/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/public/index.html`**
- The title, the single h1, the form with `novalidate`, all five fields, the labels (separate from their fields, exact text) and the filter controls all match the spec.
- `#error` has `role="alert"` and starts empty.
- There is no `<option>` and no room name in the HTML.
- `<script src="/app.js">` is the last element in `<body>`, with no type, defer or async. The inline `<style>` is allowed; it contains no URLs.

**`/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/public/app.js`**
- **Reply handling (`request`, lines 33–52):** it never rejects. Its three outcomes match the error rules:
  - A non-204 reply whose `json()` fails counts as no reply.
  - Success means exactly 200, 201 or 204.
  - The error message rule is correct (lines 21–27).
- **Startup:** `loadRooms()` and `loadList()` both call `fetch` before any `await` resolves, so the list fetch does not wait for the rooms reply.
- **Overlapping list fetches:** the counter check at line 117 comes before any change to the list or `#error`. That covers error status and no reply too.
- **Book:** it is re-enabled at line 153, the first statement after the request settles, including when `json()` fails. `preventDefault` is the first statement in the submit handler. The payload sends the raw, untrimmed values with the exact header.
- **Cancel:** no reply shows the message and does not fetch the list again. On 204 or any other status it sets `#error`, then fetches the list again.
- **Filter:** only `change` fetches the list. `Show all` sets the value to empty and fetches once, without dispatching an event.
- **List items:** `append(string, button)` gives exactly two child nodes, and the text has no trailing space. The empty case is a single text node.

**Minor nits (none blocks the pass)**
- Lines 37 and 44: `catch (failure)` never uses the binding. `catch {` would make it clear the error is deliberately turned into an outcome.
- Line 159: `showError('')` is used to clear the error. A `clearError()` helper, also used at line 174, would read more clearly.
- Line 125: the shape check only confirms each booking is an object. A booking missing a field would show `undefined` in the list text. This is a spec-silent edge case, the same kind as the one recorded in `decisions.md`.

## GRADE
Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — one IIFE with small single-purpose functions; outcome objects instead of exceptions; shallow nesting
naming: 9 — clear, consistent names; `showError('')` used to clear is a slight mismatch
duplication: 9 — shared `request`/`showFailure`/`isPlainObject` helpers; no copied logic
size: 10 — 189-line script, 52-line page; every function well under 50 lines
errors: 9 — every fetch and json failure mapped explicitly; exact spec messages; stale fetches ignored; malformed 200 bodies give a friendly generic message
tests: n/a — written by the testing section
security: 10 — all values set through textContent/append; no HTML injection; no secrets; path-only URLs
leftovers: 9 — no console or debug code; unused catch bindings remain
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/public/app.js:37 use `catch {` (unused `failure` binding)
- /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/public/app.js:44 use `catch {` (unused `failure` binding)
- /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/public/app.js:159 add a `clearError()` helper instead of `showError('')`, and use it at line 174 too
- /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/public/app.js:125 optionally also check that the booking fields are strings, so a malformed booking gives `Request failed.` instead of rendering `undefined` (record this in decisions.md if added)
